calling copyTo for a selective migration without accounting for every custom key and its replace policy
passing null to set as removal or clearing foreign keys during cleanup or migration
advancing schema version before successful migration, partially exposing a current record, or rewriting unsupported-future data
claiming atomic transactions, save timing, unload behavior, restart durability, thread safety, or Folia compatibility without target-version evidence
mixing ItemStack logical identity, similarity, or presentation-refresh policy into this generic storage concern
scenarios.failureMode: Persistent data can be misclassified, truncated, stranded on a snapshot, lost during holder conversion, overwritten across namespaces, or left partially migrated when its typed storage and lifecycle contract is implicit.

scenarios.title: Design or review evidence for a Paper plugin change
scenarios.userPrompt: Create or review a Paper plugin test plan whose evidence is strong enough for each runtime claim without relying on unsupported mocks or nondeterministic waits.
useWhen: the request asks how to test a Paper plugin feature or whether existing tests are sufficient
the change touches plugin load, commands, listeners, scheduling, persistence, inventories, packets, resources, reload, disconnect, or disable
the available choices include pure tests, mocks or fakes, MockBukkit, a loaded Paper server, or a real client
a final answer must distinguish compilation, harness coverage, runtime verification, and manual evidence
successCriteria: every material behavior and final claim names an observable boundary and minimum sufficient evidence layer
pure tests cover deterministic domain rules while mocks and fakes model only plugin-owned contracts
MockBukkit is used only for behavior supported by the selected harness and its limitations remain explicit
target-version loaded-server tests cover changed plugin descriptors, bootstrap, dependency wiring, registration, scheduler integration, reload, and disable behavior

protocol evidence covers packet transport and shape, while a real instrumented client or captured client state covers rendering, audio, input, resource-pack application, and other client-visible outcomes
time, task ordering, retries, timeouts, external responses, identifiers, and cleanup are deterministic and isolated
failure, duplicate callback, stale completion, cancellation, disconnect, partial enable, reload, disable, restart, and migration paths are tested when in scope
the final report lists exact commands, target versions, results, known baselines, skipped or unavailable checks, manual work, and a conclusion limited to completed evidence
mustAvoid: calling compilation or static analysis proof that the plugin works
mocking undocumented Paper internals and treating configured return values as runtime evidence
silently stubbing unsupported MockBukkit methods
changing bootstrap or registration without loading the plugin on a target-version server
using Thread.sleep, wall-clock polling, a live network, or shared mutable fixtures for deterministic behavior
testing asynchronous success without cancellation, stale completion, and teardown ordering
replacing a persistence adapter with memory-only storage when claiming serialization or migration correctness
using server state alone to claim a client rendered, heard, received, or applied something
reporting all tests passed without exact commands, version, failures, skips, baselines, and limitations
scenarios.failureMode: A convenient harness can verify the wrong boundary, allowing runtime, lifecycle, persistence, or client failures to escape while the implementation is reported as fully tested.

scenarios.title: Design or review Fabric Client GameTest visual evidence
scenarios.userPrompt: Create or review a reproducible Fabric Client GameTest screenshot workflow with stable cases, explicit baseline updates, artifact reconciliation, and evidence claims limited to the environment that actually ran.
useWhen: a Fabric client UI or renderer needs automated screenshot or visual-regression evidence
the test suite supports selected cases, ranges, shards, resume, or baseline updates
CI runs under a virtual framebuffer or another non-interactive display environment
a report must prove which cases ran and distinguish test, render, capture, and compare failures
successCriteria: the versioned suite definition has stable semantic case IDs, complete case metadata, and bounded readiness barriers
expected, selected, executed, passed, failed, skipped, and not-selected case sets are reconciled without treating a selected range as suite-complete

every case reported as captured, compared, or visually passed retains a full-frame artifact, earlier failures record a phase-aware expected absence, and optional crops use runtime-derived bounds verified within their source frame
compare and baseline-update are explicit separate run types and candidate baseline generation cannot satisfy a visual assertion
the manifest rejects missing, stale, duplicate, and unexpected artifacts and binds every artifact to a case, role, metadata digest, and content digest
cleanup is run-owned and idempotent, and retries cannot inherit evidence from an interrupted run
each failure preserves a primary readiness or assertion, render, capture, compare, or infrastructure phase
the final claim identifies whether evidence came from non-render assertions, a virtual-framebuffer client, or an interactive client and states what that environment does not prove
concrete Client GameTest and Loom API names are verified against current official Fabric documentation and target-version API or mappings
mustAvoid: using array positions, timestamps, or random values as durable case identity
waiting a fixed delay instead of a bounded state-specific readiness barrier
calling a selected-case, resumed range, or shard run a complete passing suite
keeping only focused crops or using one project-specific fixed crop rectangle as generic guidance
rewriting reviewed baselines during a compare run or treating a baseline-update run as a pass
ignoring stale, duplicate, unexpected, or missing artifacts in a reused output directory
reporting every failure as an image diff after an earlier assertion, render, or capture failure
calling non-render headless assertions screenshot proof or treating virtual-framebuffer evidence as physical display, hardware, input, shader, or installed-extension-set proof
substituting Paper or server GameTest guidance for the Fabric client concern
claiming one concrete Fabric client-test API spelling works across every target release
scenarios.failureMode: A screenshot suite can silently bless partial or stale output, overwrite its own oracle, and overstate CI evidence when selection, readiness, artifact ownership, failure phases, and environment limits are not explicit.

scenarios.title: Review a bounded lifecycle-owned Paper world operation
scenarios.userPrompt: Create or review a Paper operation that safely loads and mutates bounded block or entity targets across chunk and Folia region boundaries, survives unload and shutdown races, and releases every owned chunk ticket.
useWhen: the request edits, scans, drops into, moves through, removes from, or teleports across multiple chunks
the code uses getChunkAtAsync, isChunkLoaded, plugin chunk tickets, RegionScheduler, EntityScheduler, teleportAsync, or chunk lifecycle events
a block or entity operation continues across ticks, asynchronous completion, chunk unload, region handoff, or plugin disable
the review needs fixed chunk or batch limits, explicit generation policy, typed partial outcomes, idempotent retry, or ticket cleanup
successCriteria: the exact target Paper version, official API behavior sources, complete deduplicated chunk set, generation policy, chunk and target caps, per-tick and per-region budgets, timeout, and rejection rules are known before mutation

chunk acquisition never waits or blocks via Future.get or Future.join on a server main, tick, or region thread and async completion is transferred to the verified location-region or entity owner before mutation

isChunkLoaded is only a snapshot, while every required plugin ticket has bounded lifecycle ownership, sharing semantics, and exactly-once release on complete, partial, rejected, timeout, stale, unloaded, cancellation, exception, and disable

location work carries immutable world identity plus coordinates and re-resolves them in the owning region, while entity work uses the entity scheduler as its handoff and revalidates entity identity, validity, state, and operation preconditions inside the owned callback without requiring cross-region World.getEntity lookup
EntityScheduler retired callbacks only record or forward minimal terminal intent and defer entity, chunk, world, and ticket-level cleanup because the callback runs in critical code
each callback enforces target and time budgets and reports complete, partial, rejected, timeout, stale, or unloaded with bounded progress counts
physics, drops, entity movement or removal, teleport false, chunk unload, cancellation, and plugin disable are revalidated rather than inferred from scheduling or events
partial retries compare observed state with per-target progress and cannot repeat committed drops, removals, teleports, or other non-idempotent effects
Paper and Folia execution claims distinguish location-region work from entity scheduler work and never claim multi-region atomicity
mustAvoid: discovering an unbounded chunk set while world mutation is already running
letting a convenience overload choose whether missing chunks generate
treating isChunkLoaded as a residency lease
waiting or blocking via Future.get or Future.join on a server main, tick, or region thread
assuming an async API exists or completes on a particular thread without checking the target version
treating async or teleport Future completion as arbitrary-thread mutation safety or unconditional operation success
dereferencing retained Chunk, Block, BlockState, mutable Location, or Entity values outside their verified owner or treating them as current after a lifecycle change without owner-local revalidation

requiring unsafe cross-region World.getEntity lookup instead of using the entity scheduler as the entity handoff, or performing entity, chunk, world, or ticket-level cleanup inside its critical retired callback
running unbounded chunk, block, drop, or entity work in one callback
assuming plugin chunk tickets are low-cost or automatically released
using one Paper main-thread transaction model as a Folia ownership model or presenting independently scheduled regions as atomic
presenting applyPhysics=false as a general block-placement safety guarantee
treating entity unload as death or despawn
relying on events alone for complete cleanup or atomicity
retrying partial non-idempotent work without per-target reconciliation
scenarios.failureMode: Cross-chunk mutation can freeze ticks, load or pin unbounded terrain, race wrong-owner or unloaded state, leak tickets, and duplicate irreversible effects when the operation has no bounded target manifest, typed progress, reconciliation, or lifecycle owner.

scenarios.title: Review Paper custom recipe ownership, matching, and reload
scenarios.userPrompt: Create or review configurable Paper custom recipes that reconcile only plugin-owned keys, preserve exact ingredient semantics, expose partial registration failure, and keep online clients consistent across reload.
useWhen: Paper code registers shaped or shapeless recipes
recipe definitions come from configuration or can change at runtime
ingredients depend on ItemStack metadata instead of material alone
online players need late recipe-list updates or recipe-book discovery
the request changes or diagnoses recipe reload, disable, or re-enable behavior
successCriteria: every recipe has a stable plugin-owned NamespacedKey
desired definitions are fully parsed and validated before global registry mutation
reload reconciles unchanged, added, changed, and removed owned keys without clearing or resetting unrelated recipes
every add and remove result contributes to an explicit applied, rejected, restored, or partial outcome
material, exact-stack, and custom-flow ingredient identity are deliberately separated
RecipeChoice.ExactChoice is used only when full stack equality aside from amount is intended
shaped occupied bounds and slot identities or shapeless counted ingredient multisets produce target-compatible canonical match signatures
duplicate keys and distinct recipes that can match the same crafting input are rejected or explicitly resolved before registry mutation
recipe-list resend and recipe-book discovery policies are separate and target-version verified
partial failure recovers toward last-known-good owned definitions and remains observable
loaded-server and client evidence cover reload, matching, consumption, output, online visibility, disable, and re-enable
mustAvoid: calling clearRecipes or resetRecipes for plugin reload or disable
removing recipes outside the plugin-owned key set
ignoring false addRecipe or removeRecipe results
mutating the registry before all desired definitions validate
describing a sequence of global mutations as atomic
using material-only matching when metadata is part of ingredient identity
using RecipeChoice.ExactChoice for subset matching or amount-sensitive matching
checking only NamespacedKey collisions while different keys accept the same crafting input
letting declaration or iteration order silently decide between colliding recipe outputs
assuming shaped rotations, mirroring, tags, or custom-choice behavior without target-version evidence
assuming registration automatically updates every online client or discovers the recipe
claiming client visibility from server-only assertions
inventing custom recipe matching or lifecycle APIs not verified for the target version
scenarios.failureMode: A plausible recipe implementation can corrupt unrelated registry state, silently apply only part of a reload, accept unintended items, or leave online recipe lists and recipe books stale.
